A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-regression simulations and MNIST CVAE experiments, including FID results and supplementary ELBO and reconstruction-loss trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains original regression and MNIST results and adds XSUM summarization experiments, revised ELBO experiments and supplementary robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The generate–verify–retrain procedure and original model architectures remain. Appendix D.2 adds ellipsoidal and l1 verifier variants, replacing the spherical acceptance threshold with thresholds involving sqrt(xᵀA⁻¹x) and the infinity norm of x. These are limited procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: v2 adds natural-language news summarization on XSUM using SmolLM2-135M, substantially extending coverage beyond linear-regression simulations and MNIST image generation. The original domains remain.

E2.justification: The retained experiments preserve their unfiltered-retraining controls and real-data reference models. XSUM extends the filtered-versus-unfiltered comparison to another task. Newly discussed reward-optimization and RLVR methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C replaces the 20-round, 30K-to-1M ELBO schedule with 50 rounds using 5K, 30K or 50K per-round sample increments. Added protocols include 15-round XSUM retraining with ROUGE-1 filtering and greedy decoding, MNIST-specific FID embeddings, random Gaussian covariates and varied initial MNIST sample sizes.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests dependence on orthogonal covariate design, spherical verifier geometry, Inception-based FID and the small initial training set. These address distinct robustness questions absent from v1. The revised ELBO experiment also compares convergence across three synthetic-data growth schedules.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. v2 continues reporting individual trajectories without quantified experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: New XSUM results show filtered ROUGE-1 rising from approximately 0.145 to 0.167 while unfiltered retraining remains near 0.145. Appendix D adds regression and MNIST robustness results. Figure 6 replaces the earlier ELBO/reconstruction trajectories with three ELBO trajectories under changed settings. The quoted standard-FID values of 17.56 for the full-data CVAE and 21.17 for the best synthetic model remain.

T1.justification: The main theorems and proof strategy remain, with localized formal revisions. Theorem 3.1 changes its singular-value assumption from ω(sqrt(n0)) to Ω(sqrt(n0)), although Appendix B retains ω. Section 4 changes the collapse/improvement reference from the first retrained estimator to the initial estimator. Appendix D.2 adds verifier-shape derivations. Appendix A.3 incorrectly replaces the contraction expression's half-width (β−α)/2 with |(α+β)/2|.

C1.justification: The abstract extends empirical confirmation to SmolLM2-135M on XSUM. The central claims about near-term bias–variance improvements, eventual convergence to verifier knowledge and possible reversal under verifier bias are retained.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds substantive limitations concerning well-specified parametric truth and whether a unique optimal natural-language model exists. Appendix D discusses MNIST embedding suitability and explains why a generator initialized on all 60K images gains stabilization rather than improvement without stronger external knowledge. These materially qualify practical applicability.

D1.justification: v2 adds an experimental-code repository address and newly documents discriminator dropout of 0.1 and label smoothing of 0.05. It also provides implementation information for the new language-model and MNIST-embedding experiments. Most original CVAE architecture and preprocessing details remain; newly documented regularizers do not establish their absence from v1.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds a dedicated comparison with reward maximization, preference learning and RLVR, distinguishing reward optimization from ground-truth parameter recovery through binary filtering. It expands the discussion of curated-data convergence and diversity collapse, adds relevant research citations and introduces references supporting the new experiments.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and condenses related work, theorem explanations, long-term dynamics and experimental discussion. The main-text retraining scheme moves to Appendix B, theorem commentary is integrated into prose, and appendix headings and terminology are revised. These editorial changes extend beyond accommodating new results.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 3 and 4 become the four-panel Figure 3 in v2. The FID figure is relocated and partly redrawn. Figure 6 changes from a dual-axis, 20-round display to three 50-round ELBO curves. New XSUM and appendix figures add substantial visual material, including a filtered-run zoom.

improvement.justification: XSUM and Appendix D strengthen empirical coverage and address important robustness questions, while the expanded limitations improve interpretation. However, v2 introduces an error into the central convergence proof: Appendix A.3 replaces the correct interval half-width with its absolute midpoint, making the displayed conditional variance undefined for symmetric intervals used in Appendix B. The main theorem and appendix also disagree on the revised singular-value assumption. Stronger empirical support therefore coexists with weakened mathematical reliability, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
